description: Decision-scenario regression evals; assertions check decisions, not wording. Run against any rewrite of SKILL.md before merging it, and after any change that moves prose between this skill and a caller that cites it.

evals.name: the-sequence-runs-summary-walkthrough-ranking-then-gate
evals.prompt: You are executing the settle-and-merge skill (read its SKILL.md, and NOTES.md if present, from the skill directory you were given). backlog-orchestrator has found its wave settled and invoked you over its eight open PRs. It passed its resolved policy (two repositories opted into auto-merge; auto-request-settle is on) and asked for a ranking, with its cross-branch collisions and held issue set. To save time, a teammate proposes: rank the PRs with plan-merge-order first so merges can start while summarize-wave is still running, then do the summary and the decision walkthrough afterwards for the report. Question: in what order do the steps run, and why?
evals.expected_output: No. Reconcile tracker and remote state first, then summarize-wave, then act on its action points, then request the settle-outstanding-decisions walkthrough (while auto-request-settle is on), then plan-merge-order with the rulings translated into action points, then the gate and the merges, then surface the summary, the walkthrough's report and the ranking. The summary comes before the ranking because an action point can change whether something should merge at all, and the walkthrough sits between summary and ranking because a ruling changes what the ranking is computed from. Ranking first gives the user an order they may start acting on before an action point or ruling invalidates it.
assertions: The answer rejects ranking or merging before the summary
The answer orders the steps reconcile, summary, action points, walkthrough, ranking, gate, surface
The answer gives a reason for the walkthrough sitting between summary and ranking: a ruling changes what the ranking is computed from

Its DECISION and MERGE_RISK inputs do not exist until summarize-wave produces them, so an evaluation before the summary is a guess wearing the gate's name. The outstanding-item test is also wave-wide: a DECISION raised about PR-1 or PR-3 holds PR-2 too, and an unruled DECISION is outstanding. PR-2 waits for step 6.
assertions: The answer refuses to merge PR-2 before the summary runs
The answer says the gate's DECISION/MERGE_RISK inputs do not exist before summarize-wave produces them
The answer notes the outstanding-item test covers the whole wave, not only PR-2

evals.name: documented-publish-review-requires-a-fresh-round
evals.prompt: You are executing the settle-and-merge skill (read its SKILL.md, and NOTES.md if present, from the skill directory you were given). At step 6 the gate passes for PR-4, which is still a draft nobody has ever marked ready. Its repository opted into auto-merge, and its AGENTS.md says that marking a draft ready starts the repository's automated review. PR-4's existing review is clean on its current head. Question: what happens to PR-4 in this pass, and when may it merge?
evals.expected_output: It is published, not skipped: publishing is part of the merge path, so a draft whose gate opens is published by the act of merging it. The repository's own AGENTS.md says publishing starts a review, which is one of the sources that counts, so a fresh automated review round on the current head, completed after the publish, is required before the gate opens; the clean review from before the publish does not discharge it. PR-4 does not merge in this pass and the merge is not awaited inline: the PR returns to the caller and merges on a later delivered pass once that round has come back clean. If the re-review finds something, the PR is not clean and returns to ordinary repair as a ready PR.
assertions: The answer publishes PR-4 rather than skipping it for being a draft
The answer treats the AGENTS.md statement as evidence that publishing starts a review, so a fresh round after the publish is required
The answer refuses to merge in the same pass on the pre-publish review
The answer refuses an inline wait and defers the merge to a later pass

evals.name: the-closing-output-lists-unposted-held-replies
evals.prompt: You are executing the settle-and-merge skill (read its SKILL.md, and NOTES.md if present, from the skill directory you were given). The caller passed two approval-pending reply items, each a thread a person is in with its fix pushed and its one-line held reply. Questions: (a) does the closing output mention them, and with what? evals.expected_output: (a) Yes: it lists every held reply not yet posted — thread URL, fix SHA and the one-line text — separately from the decisions, so the owner can post it themselves. It also lists each fix pushed on a thread a person is in that also asks a question as 'fix pushed — thread left for you (it also asks a question)'. assertions: the closing output lists each unposted held reply with its thread URL, fix SHA and text
the answer says a later settle-outstanding-decisions run cannot recover the held text
the answer says a later re-dispatch finds the change on the head and composes a fresh held reply
